$comment: SHIPPED DEFAULT — the repo-bounded ceiling (R25, KD4, KD10). Handed to a child whose caller was an AGENT, so no human is present to answer for it. {{WORKTREE}} is substituted at launch with the job's worktree, absolute and with the leading slash removed, because a permission path is only absolute when it begins with '//' — a rule written '/Users/...' matches nothing and reads as an allow that silently is not one (measured). Three bounds, each measured against the real CLI: (1) writes and edits are scoped to the worktree, and the permission system resolves a path BEFORE matching it, so a symlink inside the tree that resolves outside falls outside the allow and is refused; (2) version-control internals and hooks are denied outright, so a job cannot leave behind something that runs on the next commit; (3) agent configuration is denied, so a job cannot widen its own ceiling or the next session's. Bash is NOT allowed: this ceiling is reached only when nobody is watching, and the same launcher's own shell permission must not leak into it — the agent entry point drops 'user' from the child's setting sources for exactly that reason. defaultMode is dontAsk so an unallowed call is REFUSED rather than queued behind a prompt nobody will answer (R9). !! MEASURED 2026-08-13, AND THIS FILE'S CENTRAL CLAIM DOES NOT HOLD. Below, this comment says Bash is NOT allowed. Through the REAL bg-agent path on the installed plugin, an unattended job ran `id -un` via Bash and wrote the true username to a deliverable, with permission_denials EMPTY and the job classified `done`. Reproduce: a contract whose task is to Bash `id -un` and write its exact stdout. It is PARTIAL, not open: the same path REFUSED `echo CEILING_BREACH_$(id -un)` (denials=1), and REFUSED WebFetch and WebSearch (denials=2). So some Bash calls are gated and some are not, and the mechanism behind the difference is NOT yet understood — command substitution is a hypothesis, not a finding. Do not rely on this ceiling to prevent shell execution until that is settled. Also measured, and wrong in the OTHER direction: a real child has NO Grep and NO Glob at all, so the entries for them in the allow list below are inert on this harness version. A residual finding that an unattended job could Grep outside the worktree was therefore never real. The general lesson, paid for twice here: a tool LIST is the model's self-report and is not evidence. Only an observed refusal, or an observed effect, is. Note the mechanisms differ in what they leave behind, measured: a call that is simply NOT ALLOWED (Bash, or a write outside the worktree) is attempted, refused, and RECORDED in the child result's permission_denials[]; a deny rule below is also attempted and refused, but leaves NO entry there, so a supervisor can only detect those by effect against a baseline. No tool is removed by a tool-level deny anywhere in this file, because a removed tool is never attempted and leaves nothing at all. To override, point SPAWN_CEILING_CONFIG_REPO at your own file; the plugin never edits your settings for you.
